## The shift {.smaller}

For decades: **you type every line.**

Agentic coding: **you describe what you want; the agent writes, runs, and fixes it; you review and decide what to keep.**

::: {.fragment}
Your role: **author → director.**
:::

::: {.fragment}
Value shifts from *syntax recall* to *clear intent, critical review, and control.*
:::

## What is an "agent"? {.smaller}

Three things, no magic:

1. **An LLM** — turns descriptions into code
2. **Tools** — read/write files, run code, search
3. **A loop** — act → observe → decide → repeat

. . .

A chatbot *answers*. An agent *acts, checks its work, and iterates* — in your real project.

## The agentic loop

```
   you ─► LLM ─► pick a tool ─► run it ─► read result
           ▲                                 │
           └──────── decide next ◄───────────┘
                  (repeat until done)
```

. . .

This loop is why an agent can debug a simulation or fix a broken join *without* you round-tripping every message.

## The landscape (mid-2026) {.smaller}

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| **Terminal / CLI agents** | **Claude Code** (this course) |
| IDE-integrated | VS Code / JetBrains, Cursor |
| Chat + code | claude.ai, ChatGPT |
| Cloud / async | PR-based coding agents |

. . .

We use Claude Code because it works in a **real git repo** — so we teach agents and version control together.

## Vocabulary {.smaller}

- **Token / context window** — what the model reads; measures memory & cost
- **Prompt** — what you ask (and asking *well*)
- **Tool call** — an action the agent takes
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — standing project instructions (Module 2)
- **Skill** — a reusable procedure (Module 4)
- **Hallucination** — plausible-but-false output → why we review

## Where it helps research

- Boilerplate & data glue
- Debugging (it runs your code + reads errors)
- Refactoring scripts into pipelines
- Simulation scaffolding
- Publication-ready figures & tables
- Methods sections, READMEs, reviewer responses

## Handle with care

- **Statistical / causal judgment** — the estimand is *yours*
- **Domain correctness** — invented parameters & citations
- **Irreversible actions** — deleting, force-pushing
- **Confidential data** — know your IRB / data-use rules

## The one rule {.center}

::: {.r-fit-text}
Never merge what you haven't reviewed.
:::

. . .

Fast + confident + sometimes wrong → keep a review step. That's why the next big module is **git**.

## Recap {.smaller}

- Agent = **LLM + tools + a loop**
- You **direct and review**, you don't type
- Strong on boilerplate/debugging/figures; weak on judgment you must own
- Safe only if you **review before you keep**

. . .
